title: Lease offers state a purchase option price but no labeled residual value or adjusted capitalized cost

statute: FTC Act §5 (15 U.S.C. §45); FTC Pricing Transparency FAQs Q4, Q5, Q6; CA Civil Code §1784.41(a) (CARS Act, operative 2026-10-01)
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: The page text alone cannot show font size or card layout, and the Disclosure expander and Get New Century Offer button were not opened on the listing. Every new-vehicle card captured presents MSRP as the only price, with the $85 doc fee and $37 EVR fee listed as add-ons and never summed. Show a summed selling price (for the 840i: $98,647 before tax and license, or the California equivalent including the document processing charge) as the headline number on each card, keep MSRP secondary and labeled, and confirm Get New Century Offer does not reveal a different or lower price only after contact info is submitted (CA-CARS-026 once operative 2026-10-01).

title: Used-vehicle finance disclosure labels dealer price as 'MSRP'

statute: CA Business & Professions Code §17500, §17501; CA Vehicle Code §11713(a)
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: The discount math comes from price figures read from the page, not labeled text, so confirm the List Price and Dealer Discount lines on the live vehicle page. For this used 2026 X3 the page's own pricing figures ($58,375 less a $4,915 discount = $53,460) show $53,460 is the dealer selling price, not a manufacturer sticker. The listing therefore prices the vehicle $4,915 above what the finance disclosure calls MSRP, then discounts it back down to it. The finance disclosure template appears to fill the MSRP field with the used selling price, which misstates a reference price shoppers rely on. Remove the MSRP field from used and CPO finance disclosures (or fill it with the verified original MSRP, clearly labeled as the original new-vehicle MSRP) and have Team Velocity fix the template sitewide.

title: No reference to the CARS Act 3-day used-vehicle cancellation right
quote: Pre-owned vehicle pricing includes all offers and incentives. Tax, Title and Tags not included in vehicle prices shown and must be paid by the purchaser.
statute: CA Civil Code §1784.43 (CARS Act, SB 766, operative 2026-10-01)
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: Forward-looking: this is not a violation today. Full text of the used listing page was not captured, so the absence rests on the pre-owned vehicle page disclosures and a search of every page reviewed, which found no cancellation, 3-day, or all-sales-final language. From 2026-10-01, used vehicles priced $50,000 or less (for example the 2024 X3 at $34,785) carry a 3-day right to cancel. The main disclosure is required at the point of sale, so this is a best-practice gap on the website. Consider a short line on used inventory and vehicle page templates noting the statutory 3-day cancellation right for eligible vehicles, and make sure no 'all sales final' or 'as-is' copy is added.
